classification.difficultyReason: Read four temperatures directly from uniformly subdivided Celsius scales.

content.prompt: Determine the readings for each of the thermometers shown below.

spec.description: Vertical thermometer with one-degree subdivisions, longer five-degree ticks and labels every ten degrees from −60 to 50. Liquid reaches zero. Decorative enclosure omitted; ordinary outlines use black.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid and complete scale are permanent givens; no numerical reading is supplied separately.

answer.worked: The top of the liquid is level with the $0$ tick, so the temperature is $0^{\circ}\mathrm C$.

spec.description: Same Celsius scale as part a; liquid surface is halfway between −20 and −30. Decorative enclosure omitted; ordinary outlines use black.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid and scale remain visible in the question; reading appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The liquid is halfway between $-20^{\circ}\mathrm C$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm C$, so the temperature is $-25^{\circ}\mathrm C$.

spec.description: Same Celsius scale as part a; liquid surface is halfway between zero and −10. Decorative enclosure omitted; ordinary outlines use black.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid and scale remain visible in the question; reading appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The liquid is halfway between $0^{\circ}\mathrm C$ and $-10^{\circ}\mathrm C$, so the temperature is $-5^{\circ}\mathrm C$.

spec.description: Same Celsius scale as part a; liquid surface is halfway between −10 and −20. Decorative enclosure omitted; ordinary outlines use black.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid and scale remain visible in the question; reading appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The liquid is halfway between $-10^{\circ}\mathrm C$ and $-20^{\circ}\mathrm C$, so the temperature is $-15^{\circ}\mathrm C$.
